questions.question: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. When they left for Mexico, their house was in good condition than it is now
questions.questionHtml:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

When they left for Mexico, their house was in good condition than it is now
questions.solution: The word 'better' will be used as the comparative degree of 'good' because the sentence is making a comparison. For the comparative degree of 'good', the correct form is 'better'. The sentence means that when they left for Mexico, their house was in a better condition than it is now. Therefore, the correct answer is 'better'. For example— The food is better today than it was yesterday.

questions.question: For the four-sentence (S1 to S4) paragraph below, sentences S1 and S4 are given. From the options P, Q, R and S select the appropriate sentences for S2 and S3, respectively. S1) The news about China’s economic slowdown has caused mixed reactions. P) China's sovereignty and maritime claims based on the nine-dotted line on the map are "invalid," said the statement, which cited Pham Thu Hang, the spokesperson for Vietnam's foreign affairs ministry Q) China released the map so publishers, companies and others have an official version to reference. R) China, for long, had been worried about fears of a slowdown and a middle-income trap. S) Now, there are fears of deflation which may bring bad news for China and the rest of the world. S4) Thus, understanding the causes and the magnitude of China’s present-day economic challenges is essential.
questions.questionHtml:
For the four-sentence (S1 to S4) paragraph below, sentences S1 and S4 are given. From the options P, Q, R and S select the appropriate sentences for S2 and S3, respectively.
S1) The news about China’s economic slowdown has caused mixed reactions.
P) China's sovereignty and maritime claims based on the nine-dotted line on the map are "invalid," said the statement, which cited Pham Thu Hang, the spokesperson for Vietnam's foreign affairs ministry
Q) China released the map so publishers, companies and others have an official version to reference.
R) China, for long, had been worried about fears of a slowdown and a middle-income trap.
S) Now, there are fears of deflation which may bring bad news for China and the rest of the world.

S4) Thus, understanding the causes and the magnitude of China’s present-day economic challenges is essential.
questions.solution: Based on the theme set by S1 and S4, sentences R and S (Option C) seem to be the most appropriate choices for S2 and S3 respectively. They provide context about China's longstanding concerns and the potential implications, fitting in with the theme of the economic slowdown.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I always prefer a small, cosy cottage ______ a high-rise apartment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I always prefer a small, cosy cottage ______ a high-rise apartment.
questions.solution: 'To' will be used because with "prefer," when comparing two things, the correct preposition is 'to'. The sentence conveys that a "small, cosy cottage" is preferred over a "high-rise apartment," making 'to' appropriate here. Whereas 'from' refers to a source, 'for' is used for purpose, and 'than' is used with comparatives, which don't fit in this context.

questions.solution: B) The correct spelling of the underlined word "susteinability" is "sustainability," which means “the ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level, especially without depleting natural resources” (स्थिरता, टिकाऊपन).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Gandhi’s ways of life, if followed in their entirety, will aid us in the creation of a society of peace and _______.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Gandhi’s ways of life, if followed in their entirety, will aid us in the creation of a society of peace and _______.
questions.solution: ‘Harmony’ is the correct choice because it means a state of peaceful coexistence and agreement, which aligns with the idea of a peaceful and ideal society as described in the sentence. The word “peace” and “harmony” complement each other, making this option contextually appropriate. Discord: It means disagreement or conflict, which is the opposite of “peace” and does not fit the positive tone of the sentence. Agitation: It refers to unrest or disturbance, which contradicts the concept of “peace” and is inappropriate here. Cacophony: It means a harsh, discordant noise, which again opposes the idea of a peaceful society.

The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The train is running / late by six hours / so it / cannot make over the time.

cannot make over the time
late by six hours

questions.solution: 'cannot make up the time' will be used instead of 'cannot make over the time' because 'make up time' means to compensate for lost time, whereas 'make over' means to transfer ownership or renovate something, which is incorrect in this context; Like— The train is running late by six hours, so it cannot make up the time

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
P) Recently, there was a function to release a book written by an architect in Kerala.
Q) Written in an easy style, the book was a pleasure to read.
R) The book was a collection of memories of the author’s travels to exotic places and about his blissful moments watching nature.
S) There was nothing about his personal background or achievements in life.
questions.solution: P: Sentence P begins with the word "Recently", indicating a starting point or introduction to an event. This suggests that P is the beginning of the paragraph.

questions.question: Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank . “The Union has to activate itself,” Justice Hima Kohli, who is heading the Supreme Court Bench hearing the case against Patanjali Ayurved and its leaders Acharya Balkrishna and Baba Ramdev, observed on April 23 in the context of the government not having taken any action against the company for publishing advertisements _____1_____ untested, pseudoscientific cures for COVID-19, diabetes, and other conditions. The Bench also took cognisance of a report that the baby formula Nestlé sells in India contains more sugar than its corresponding product in Europe, and expanded the Patanjali Ayurved matter’s remit to include all fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies publishing misleading advertisements. India has been recording a surge in non-communicable diseases (NCDs) ____2____the easy availability of ultra-processed foods, together with _____3____lifestyles. Manufacturers have also been known to include some vitamins, say, in order to escape scrutiny, but their product is still ‘junk’. In the last month, the apex court has sought public ____4_____from Patanjali Ayurved et al. for advertising misleading claims even after the Court directed them to stop; the Bench ____5____ the defendants for publishing a diminutive advertisement. There is some uncertainty now over whether the Court will accept the latest apology, but herein lies the rub. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
